_meta.change_point_rule: Every outfit switch is listed in its character's change_points: after_event = last event in the old outfit's range; effective_from_event = first event the new outfit is on screen. All costume switches in this film happen off screen between scenes, so storyboard/shot-planning never needs a switch inside a generation group. Wet, sooty, leaf-strewn or accessory states are NOT outfit changes: they are variants listed under the outfit and their on/off events are in the character's variant_points for 07-directing/continuity-planning.
global_rules: Period lock 1862 (style CR-002): natural fabrics only (cotton, muslin, wool, silk, velvet, linen, leather, straw); hooks, buttons, laces and ties only; no zips, plastics, synthetic sheen or post-1862 cuts.

SUP-002 / SUP-010 / XA-magic-02 (amended BIB-0027): talking animals, the Gryphon and the Mock Turtle are photoreal CGI animals and creatures. They wear only the garments the text gives them, made to 1862 pattern and tailored to the animal's anatomy: the White Rabbit's waistcoat (with collar and bow, and the herald tabard at the trial), and the Footmen's livery and powdered hair. Every other animal outfit is 'unclothed' (visual_en states it plainly; there is no separate costume sheet, only the character sheet.png). Species is carried by the CGI anatomy (04-creatures/creature, 03-characters/appearance), never by costume cues. There are no humans in animal costume, no masks and no cartoon faces. Human dream-figures and the card figures (SUP-004) remain human performers in the costumes below, which are unchanged.

WR-010 / XA-magic-08: the Art Nouveau / Mucha design language belongs to the dream environments only. Every costume, including those worn inside Art Nouveau sets, stays 1862-based: no Art Nouveau ornament, whiplash embroidery, halo collars or Mucha-style drapery on any garment.
SUP-004 card figures: the House of Hearts pack shares one card-back design, 'crimson-and-cream lattice card-back pattern with a small heart rosette', on the back of every tabard or panel (ch008-p16).

Palette accents (style.json palette_logic.accent_rules): cornflower blue is Alice's alone; Hearts crimson belongs only to the House of Hearts household (Queen, King, Knave, gardeners, soldiers, officers, executioner, Fish-Footman, royal children, the White Rabbit's herald tabard). Visiting monarchs and courtiers of Diamonds use scarlet, brick or coral, never Hearts crimson.

CR-010 / DEF-p3-char-index-902 / SUP-014: no axe, block, sword, noose or any execution device is part of any costume, and none is named in any visual_en (negation words are also kept out of visual_en; bans live in prohibited_in_prompt).
Size changes (SUP-003) never change a costume: forced-perspective scaled sets carry the size; production builds matching duplicate costumes for any scaled double.

Negation discipline for unclothed outfits: their visual_en uses only the positive phrase 'unclothed and unadorned: the bare natural <animal>, wearing nothing'. Specific bans (clothing, human in costume, masks, cartoon faces) live in prohibited_in_prompt.
Weapons and hand props (pocket watch, fan, trumpet, scroll, hookah, paintbrush, slates, sack, batons, wands, teacup, pepper-box) belong to 06-art/prop and are not part of any visual_en.

The King's, Queen's and White Rabbit's spectacles are costume for the same reason and stay as outfit variants (COS-010, COS-008, COS-007); the White Rabbit's white kid gloves and fan are the opposite case and stay props (PROP-white-kid-gloves-and-fan).
